posts.name: NinjaMonkey
posts.cooked:
Now that we finally have the complete (pre-Oblivaeon) Darkwatch team in the video game I've been trying to figure out how to get them to work together. Their base powers don't seem to provide much synergy aside from Setback being able to mitigate some of the damage Nightmist deals herself and Nightmist being able to stack her deck so that Fumbling Fool won't negatively affect her. Darkwatch Fixer punches hard and than breaks his team's stuff, and Darkwatch Expatriette boosts her own damage by 1 until the end of next turn.

So my question is, what are some of the strategies used to transform this team from a bunch of individuals into a well oiled machine like the Freedom V and the Prime Wardens?

Combo's I've already discovered either here or in play:

[Mr. Fixer]Jack Handle (Dual Crowbars) + [Setback]Friendly Fire

[Setback]Wrong Time and Place + [Nightmist]Obliveon

[Setback]Wrong Time and Place + [Nightmist]Any self damaging spell

Some strategies I've figured out through play:

Enlightenment and Surprising Fortune works nicely for equipment starved Mr. Fixer and Expatriette.

Turn of Events can help provide a nice little damage boost for a fully loaded Expatriette the turn before she Unloads.

A 4/4 Obliveon turns into a 20 point nuke to the main villain with Wrong Time and Place and a pool full of tokens [16 minimum] (easier with Friendly Fire to help mitigate the token loss [8 minimum]).

Speed Load keeps Mr. Fixer in ammo to destroy.

posts.cooked:
Expatriette and Setback are both extrememly Fixer-Friendly.
As you mentioned, Mr. F loves Speed Loading, but also Expat has so many guns that it’s usually ok to destroy some here and there. Fixer reciprocates by playing Salvage Yard to get them all back.
On Setback’s part, notice that a sum total of ZERO of his cards are limited. This means you can throw out multiple copies of Looking Up or Surprising Fortune just so they can be destroyed. And of course there’s the damage combos that you’ve already noticed.
Nightmist and Fixer are friends too. With all the cards she puts into her own trash, she loves a good Salvage. She also can Enlighten Expatriette so that you have a better chance of getting the guns and ammo you really want. Plus, all of them have cards to reduce or redirect that Oblivion damage.

posts.cooked:
Although learning new ways to synergize with other heroes is always interesting, I'd like to keep this discussion focused on games played with only members of the Darkwatch team.

With Darkwatch Nightmist, I've found the normal strategy of hide behind the Amulet just isn't as effective. I normally prioritize Master of Magic with her over the Amulet and tend to use her Elder Ring more. With Setback's Mitigate triggered before her turn I find I don't have to many issues with her self damage. I have started to use more of her cards for their actual effect instead of as food for the Amulet.

I'm learning her base power is more than just stacking the deck in your favor. It's about drilling 3 cards deep into your deck to quickly find a card which will be useful for the situation. and than stacking your deck. Setback have Fumbling Fool and you don't see anything useful? Pick the best of the worst to put on top for your draw and place the worst (looking at you Mist of Time) to be your top card. Now when it comes back to Nightmist she'll have 2 new cards to choose from. 3 if you've used the sparkle of the last card to cast a spell.

I hadn't considered the non-limited nature of Setbacks deck. He and Expat would be pretty good for feeding Fixer.

Mr. Fixer (any form) + Crowbar + Nightmist with Amulet of the Elder Gods:

posts.name: Braithwhite
posts.cooked:
I've found that the team order matters a great deal for DW. 

Expat goes first to mark targets, debuff enemies, or to set up her next round (if she has no guns). This lets her get the most benefit from the team members that allow for card draw early on in the game, as well as giving fixer more fodder for the bitter strike. As a side note, I've found that it can be immensely useful to use Cryo ammo on Setback or Nightmist every so often- keeps them from hurting themselves or the team. Especially with a 1 point Oblivion, or if nightmist has an elder ring out. 

Setback goes next. He's got a bit of everything, so he can clean up after expat, feed fixer, remove pesky ongoings, heal the team, and (if you get lucky) put out a stupefying amount of damage. I prefer to use his base power on Nightmist- it allows DW nightmist to be a lot riskier and more aggressive. Turn of events needs to be used judiciously, but pick your moment and you'll get a LOT out of it. With DW Setback, I tend to prioritize surprising fortune, since it gives more cards to those who need it.  But you always need to be prepared to adjust to circumstances with Setback.  Getting locked into one style or searching for that one perfect card tends to backfire.  

DW nightmist requires planning. You are going to be using her spells a LOT more, so Master of Magic is a huge boon early on. It's going to be tempting to go into must form to build up a large hand, but (in general) try to resist the impulse to hide. DW nightmist is all about thinking one step ahead, so if you use that Mist Form, have a plan for getting out of it. Unlike regular Nightmist, DW doesn't really shine as the last hero standing. You can, but you'll run out of cards faster, which limits your survivability. Her enlightens work wonders on Fixer and expat, and you can get a LOT of mileage out of the book early on. Basically, once you have spells, go on the attack. DW Setback will help keep you safe from your own damage, feed you extra cards, and heal you by cashing out. In return, support your team with raw damage, mist form tanking, and support in the form of enlightened card draws or astral enemy deck scouting. Just resist the urge to hide. 

DW fixer goes last. This lets him scavenge ongoings and puts him in prime position to benefit from unexpected Setback antics (like fumbling fool discarding a great tool when you have a salvage yard), gain cards from allies, and finish off enemies that were wounded by teammates. Go with the flow. Play whatever hits the hardest, and (unless you have a specific plan of attack), focus entirely on offense against the highest HP target. Eat your own things first (unless you have a tool or style you like), and occasionally whack your teammates with the crowbars to amp up your damage in the absence of other villain targets. 

This specific configuration gives Dark Watch a lot more flexibility and synergy. Or at least that's what I've found. They aren't unbeatable, but they are a lot nastier than they might initially seem, and you can take on just about any enemy (though fighting in Rook City always is harder!). I tend to find that Setback is the key for the entire team- he is a marvelous support and damage dealer... And if he's doing well the team will prosper. If he doesn't... well, that's what enlightenment or the occasional crowbar is for.

I see the variants as addition by subtraction. They take away the usual crutches and force you to apply a new strategy.

With DW Nightmist you can no longer spend your time hiding behind the amulet, hoarding cards for discards instead of using them. If you do this with DW Nightmist of course she’ll suck.
With this version of Nightmist Master of Magic is prioritized over the amulet, Tome of Elder Magic keeps you in spells, Enlightenment now gets used on other team members, Elder Ring actually gets played, Scouring Mists isnt a 4 letter word and Oblivion is just so much better when you can contol it.

With DW Fixer, sure you’re destroying 1 or 2 cards each round, but honestly by mid-game who doesnt have spare crap to destroy? Also Jackhandle + Grease Monkey Fist + Harmony + Bloody Knuckles (safely destroyed after or held so that Setback can let him do it again)…nuff said.

With DW Expat, honestly I dont see much difference except you dont get setup as fast. That damage boost can be pretty nice when combined with the machine gun and shock rounds. Or during an Unload.

With DW Setback, as much as people disrespect it, Mitigate is useful for Nightmist to limit her self damage or for Mr. Fixer to lower damage just enough to trigger Driving Mantis. Admittedly that last is highly situational. Also with DW Setback you’re never in danger of accidently destroying anyone elses stuff or killing yourself with a Cause and Effect.

No question that Harmony + Jack Handle + Grease Monkey fist is beastly with DW fixer, and probably worth the extra card cost, but a couple of things to keep in mind: First, without someone granting you extra card plays, the earliest you can have that combo is turn 3, and that’s if you’re lucky enough to get all three of those cards by then (which you usually won’t be). Also, while many heroes have excellent one-shots and a few have an abundance of low-value ongoings/equipments, ongoing and equipment cards tend to be a hero’s strongest, most important cards, so simply saying that it costs “one more card” is misleading. It’s also worth pointing out that his power doesn’t just cost an extra card, it costs an extra card play, which is a major tempo hit. What’s more, to get them all three out at the same time, you either have to skip your power phase in previous rounds, or destroy another hero’s card, which slows down their setup during the crucial early turns. Most of the other heroes who require significant setup time before they can start to contribute much (Absolute zero, nightmist, setback, scholar) also have consistent ways of extending their survivability through lots of healing and/or DR. Fixer has Grease Gun, which is awesome, but it’s a once-in-a-while thing, not usually something he can focus on without help. DW Fixer definitely has his uses, but the cost of having to destroy a card in order to contribute is steep.
